pattern-selector.why: the activation design was chosen on purpose: a portable ESK_ENFORCE=1 flag plus per-session derivation from the payload session_id (over a committed machine-specific path), and a detection trust model (tamper made visible, not prevented) over an admin-only managed-settings baseline; forces and the rejected options are in ADR-0101.
pattern-selector.what: built always-on/esk-paths.mjs (the per-session resolver) and the session-setup self-test; recorded the choice and alternatives in ADR-0101.
quotes: the structure that fits the forces this system will actually face, chosen on purpose

architectural-decision-records.why: the activation layer and the honest trust model are a significant decision; the choice, both operator-selected options, and the rejected alternatives are recorded in the same change.
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: the install, self-test, waiver, and traversal behaviors are specified as executable scenarios across operator and agent audiences and happy/error/adverse/negative/boundary paths, tagged, logged, and reconciled against the datastore.
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: added 9 scenarios to the apply feature and a step file driving the real installer, self-test, waivers, and the session-id traversal defense; regenerated the datastore; the full chain is green at 82 scenarios.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to judgment.

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: the activation layer, self-test, and installer are proven at the lowest level that catches the bug: unit and integration tests that spawn the real scripts with crafted inputs.
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: added test/esk-paths.test.mjs, test/session-setup.test.mjs, test/esk-enforce-install.test.mjs, and activation/waiver/fail-closed tests to test/finish-check.test.mjs; wired them into the test list.
quotes: Test at the lowest level that can catch the bug

verifiable-quality-gates.why: the enforcement is itself a gate, so every new block/deny/warn branch carries a test that fails when it is neutralized: a no-op resolver flips the fail-closed cases, a no-op self-test flips the tamper/waiver-surfacing cases, and a no-op installer flips the registration/drift cases.
verifiable-quality-gates.what: wrote discriminating tests for fail-closed-on-missing-session, operator waiver surfacing, agent-cannot-self-waive, the installer drift/opt-in, and the session-id traversal defense.
quotes: test must FAIL when the check is replaced by a no-op

skeptical-audit.why: the trust model is stated honestly rather than overclaimed: the docs say removal is made visible, not prevented, and the fresh-context review caught an overclaim (a forged waiver was said to be detected when nothing read the waivers file), which was fixed by implementing the detection rather than softening to a false claim.
skeptical-audit.what: framed the detection-not-prevention limit in ADR-0101/README/records doc and made session-setup actually surface every operator waiver so the visibility claim is true.
quotes: If you cannot attach all three, you do not assert it

judge-arch.why: a fresh-context review of the whole change ran against the four questions and found 2 findings + 3 low + 1 nit, all fixed before the PR and recorded in the append-only review log.
judge-arch.what: ran judge-arch in fresh context, fixed every finding (overclaim, fail-open, duplicated derivation, self-test gap, canary scope, wording), and appended the review entry.
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion. Every review does all of them.

release-deployment-safety.why: enforcement ships dark: --enforce is opt-in and a plain install is byte-identical, the wiring is idempotent and additive, and the marker keeps enforcement on across reconciles - deploy kept apart from release, with an install-time canary before it goes live.
release-deployment-safety.what: added the opt-in --enforce path, idempotent withEnforcement, the marker.enforce stickiness, and the enforcement canary to esk-init.mjs.
quotes: Dark-launch: ship the code off, turn it on for internal users, then 1 percent

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: the derivation rule is kept in one place (the shared resolver) rather than copied into each hook, and the hooks stay single-responsibility and fail closed; the simpler shape that meets the requirement was chosen on purpose.
enterprise-architecture-standards.what: centralized per-session path derivation in esk-paths.resolvePath and routed finish-check's waiver and derived-receipt paths through it (removing the duplicated copies).
quotes: Simplicity that meets the real requirement is a core principle, not a shortcut.

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: the session_id flows into a filesystem path, a real injection/traversal surface; it is validated at the edge (isSafeSession rejects separators and traversal), no derived path can escape the base store, an unresolvable id fails closed, and a forged operator waiver is surfaced - the control that stops the attack is stated and tested by a @security scenario.
owasp-secure-coding-bdd.what: hardened esk-paths.isSafeSession/resolvePath against a crafted session id and added the @security 'a crafted session id cannot escape the per-session store' scenario driving the real finish-check.
quotes: Each per-sheet file states the real attack the control stops

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: this change stores no personal or regulated data; the per-session store holds small operational JSON files (records, selections, waivers, a block counter), not user data, so there is no data class, retention, or deletion duty here.

sre-operational-readiness.why: no running service or endpoint is added; the install-time canary and the loop-safety escalation are covered by the installer and finish-check tests, not by SLIs/alerts/runbooks.

arch-encode.why: no greppable mistake was caught that needs a new arch-gate forbid rule; the judge-arch findings were fixed in code and pinned by discriminating tests, which is the right mechanism here.

universal-accessibility-wcag.why: no user interface; the only human-facing output is plain-text operator messages and the SessionStart additionalContext string.

universal-browser-device-support.why: no browser or device surface; these are Node hooks and an installer.

usability-ux-universal-design.why: no end-user UI; the install summary and the self-test warnings are written in plain language naming the missing item and its fix, but there is no interactive surface to design.
